newsitem.title: USA: Scientists identify remains of U.S. A-10 pilot.
newsitem.headline: Scientists identify remains of U.S. A-10 pilot.

text.p: Scientists have confirmed that human remains found at the site where a U.S. Air Force A-10 attack jet crashed in Colorado were those of the pilot, Capt. Craig Button, the Air Force said on Monday.
The wreckage of Button's jet was found on April 20 on a Rocky Mountain peak after the aircraft disappeared on April 2 loaded with bombs.

Fragmentary human remains were recovered from the snow-covered wreckage on Friday. The Air Force said they had been "positively identified" using DNA testing by scientists at the Armed Forces Institute of Pathology in Washington.

The warplane disappeared during a routine training mission, and Air Force officials have been at a loss to explain why Button veered northeast into Colorado, some 850 miles (1,360 km) away from a training exercise in Arizona.
Officials at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base in Arizona said Col. Barry Barksdale, commander of the 355th Wing, notified Button's family Sunday.
The Air Force has appointed a board of officers to investigate the accident.
